result.title: Is a Description Worth a Thousand Demonstrations? Specificity and Reliability of Task Descriptions in In-Context Learning
result.summary: A prompt for in-context learning (ICL) can describe a task in addition to, or instead of, demonstrating it through examples. Yet how task descriptions work remains poorly understood theoretically. Through the Bayesian view of ICL, we model descriptions as informative priors characterized by their specificity and reliability. We adapt the effective sample size (ESS) from Bayesian statistics, quantifying a description's predictive value as an equivalent number of demonstrations. For in-context linear regression, we show that a reliable description's ESS grows with its specificity and with the task's dimension. A description that may be irrelevant, however, gains little from its specificity unless demonstrations are given. In practice, do in-context learners use descriptions as a Bayes-optimal predictor would? Our experiments show that meta-trained Transformers come close to the Bayes-optimal ESS when tested on their training distribution. Pretrained language models, however, make too little use of highly specific descriptions when answering without reasoning; most of them closely match the Bayes-optimal predictor only when reasoning is enabled. These results extend the Bayesian analysis of ICL from demonstrations to descriptions.

AI.brief_summary: 该文从贝叶斯视角把 in-context learning 中的任务描述建模为具有特异性和可靠性的先验，用 effective sample size（ESS）衡量描述相当于多少示例，并在上下文线性回归及元训练 Transformer、预训练语言模型上检验其是否按贝叶斯最优方式使用描述，以及推理开启的作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉工作，但其用 ESS 量化「描述作为先验」的预测价值、并区分可靠性与推理开启后的使用差异，可供核查 VLM 中文字提示或视觉证据是否真正影响 latent 推理状态时借鉴。
